Restaurants are running out of hands. And the hardest part isn't the kitchen... it's the last ten meters. Finding the right table, without spilling a drop.
So we built Tableside. A humanoid that hears "table three"... and gets it there.
It sees with its own camera, and remembers what it has seen, and how sure it is. When it isn't sure, it doesn't guess. It looks again.
Carrying is learned too: PPO cut tray slip from eight centimeters to three. And it carries with its own hands, under real contact physics.

Then we fine-tuned two vision-language-action models on the robot's own sensor data. SmolVLA kept improving, step by step. NVIDIA's GR00T got worse on held-out data, and we're showing you that too. Neither beats our planner... yet.
All built in one day, by two AI engineers: Codex on simulation and training, Claude on perception and navigation.

This is the real K1 walking policy in MuJoCo, carrying the tray in its own hands. No markers. No simulator position. Just its camera, a gyro, and its joints. It finds the table... slows down... and stops, without spilling a thing. Next stop: a real robot.
